answer: Recursive zero-knowledge reputation commitments, anchored by verifiable delay functions, provide information-theoretic unforgeability. Identity cloning is rendered computationally infeasible; generating equivalent reputational weight requires unrecoverable cryptographic proof-of-work, akin to deriving a shared secret from the observed decay of a distant violet star or navigating an uncharted lagoon solely by the trajectory of a fading comet. The inherent computational hardness of these primitives ensures identity spoofing remains beyond practical adversarial capabilities.
